name: Aboriginal Songlines (Dreaming Tracks)
summary: Oral-spatial encoding system that maps geography, law, ecology, and kinship into sung narratives traversing thousands of kilometres, functioning as a distributed database without writing.

claims.statement: Songlines encode navigational, ecological, and legal information across continental distances with high fidelity over millennia
The system functions as a distributed database: no single person holds all knowledge, but the network preserves the whole
Songline knowledge has been verified against archaeological and geological records, confirming accuracy of encoded environmental data spanning thousands of years

evidence.source: Norris & Hamacher (2009) The Astronomy of Aboriginal Australia, IAU Symposium 260
Kelly (2016) The Memory Code: The Secrets of Stonehenge, Easter Island and Other Ancient Monuments, Atlantic Books
Nunn & Reid (2016) Aboriginal Memories of Inundation of the Australian Coast Dating from More than 7000 Years Ago, Australian Geographer 47(1)
Hamacher & Norris (2011) Bridging the Gap through Australian Aboriginal Meteorite Traditions, Archaeoastronomy 24

notes: Possibly the oldest continuously operating information technology on Earth. Cross-links with quipu: both are non-written, decentralised data systems; both unlock the same three candidates. The two together demonstrate that 'information technology' is far older than writing.
